linkedin.title: This Week in Finance & Tech
linkedin.body:
Tech giants are doubling down on AI integration. Meta is launching a dedicated Mac app for its AI chatbot. The software can view your open windows to provide suggestions or create content, and it supports system-wide dictation. Meanwhile, chipmaker Cerebras is hoping a new specialized chip will help its stock recover after a difficult post-IPO period. They believe their hardware can outperform standard graphics processing units as AI agents become more common.

However, these technologies bring privacy concerns. Reports are surfacing of people being secretly filmed by users wearing Meta smartglasses in private settings like homes and concerts, sparking a wider debate about personal privacy in public spaces.

In the corporate world, the potential merger between Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery remains uncertain. Prediction market traders currently estimate a 1-in-4 chance that the deal will fail, as legal challenges from 12 states continue to complicate the acquisition.

Elsewhere, luxury markets and retail habits are making headlines. A Ferrari electric vehicle recently sold at auction for $40 million, though the car's design has faced criticism from those who feel it strays too far from the brand's classic aesthetic. In a different corner of the economy, Wetherspoons customers in London are reacting positively to a new ban on speakerphone calls and loud music in some of the chain's pubs, suggesting a growing appetite for quieter public spaces.

Finally, the debate over climate policy and the economy continues. While some political figures suggest ignoring climate concerns to protect economic growth, others argue that such a stance is not only dangerous but ultimately damaging to long-term financial stability.

instagram.title: California oil pipeline cleared to resume operations

slides.headline: California oil pipeline cleared to resume operations
slides.subtitle: A federal judge ruled the Santa Barbara system can restart

slides.explanation: This pipeline runs along the coastline off Santa Barbara. It has been the center of a long-running dispute between state regulators, environmental groups, and federal authorities.

slides.headline: The federal government pushed to reopen the line
slides.explanation: While California officials and environmental groups fought to keep the pipeline shut, the Trump administration previously ordered its reopening. This ruling upholds that federal order
We verified this report across three independent outlets, including The Guardian and France 24. Their agreement confirms the legal status of the pipeline despite conflicting state and

instagram.caption:
A federal judge has ruled that an oil pipeline off the coast of Santa Barbara can continue to operate.

This decision comes despite strong opposition from California state regulators and environmental groups who wanted the system shut down.

The case highlights a deeper conflict between federal and state authority. While the state sought to stop the system from resuming operations, a prior federal order had mandated its reopening.

The ruling allows the infrastructure to remain active for now, keeping the legal and environmental debate alive. How do you think states should balance federal mandates with local environmental concerns?

story.title: Controversial California oil pipeline can continue to operate, judge rules
story.summary: State sought to stop system off coast of Santa Barbara from resuming operations after Trump ordered its reopening A controversial oil pipeline can continue to operate off the California coast after a judge gave it the green light this week, despite the opposition of state regulators and environmental groups. The system off the coast of Santa Barbara resumed operations earlier this year for the first time in more than a decade after Donald Trump ordered Sable Offshore Corporation to reopen it, citing US energy needs during the war in Iran. story_card.headline: Google Discover gets AI-powered feed customization
story_card.standfirst: You will soon be able to describe exactly what content you want to see in your Google app

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Google is adding a feature that lets you customize your Discover feed using natural language.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: The app previously relied on automated algorithms that you had little control over.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: AI will now remember your specific preferences, making your daily feed truly personal.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Look for the new option in the three-dot menu as the update rolls out in the coming days.

story_card.caption:
Google is updating the Discover feed in the Google app to let users customize content with AI.

You can now describe your interests directly to the app instead of just relying on its guesses. It will remember these preferences for future visits to keep your feed relevant. This update is hitting devices over the next few days.
